title: Finite-cover connectedness criterion for etale module sections
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Assume that for every finite morphism $h:X\prime\to X$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and every irreducible closed subset $C\subseteq X\prime$, the intersection $C\cap h^{-1}(i(Z))$ is nonempty and connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]. For every commutative coefficient ring $\Lambda$ and every sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], the canonical inverse-image restriction [def-weil-pbc-finite-section-pullback] $\Gamma(X,F)\to\Gamma(Z,i^{-1}F)$ is an isomorphism of $\Lambda$-modules.

source.place: Lemma 59.82.2; spectral input at Tag 09ZG, Lemma 59.82.4

proof.text: Let h:X'→X be finite. Its source is quasi-compact and quasi-separated since finite morphisms are quasi-compact and separated and these properties compose; hence X' is spectral. The base change i' is a closed immersion, and the pullback image formula identifies its image with h⁻¹(range i). The assumed intersection condition therefore holds for this closed subset of X'.

source.place: Lemma 59.82.2; spectral input at Tag 09ZG, Lemma 59.82.4

proof.text: For each point x of X', the closure of {x} is irreducible closed. The hypothesis makes its intersection with the image of i' nonempty and connected. The spectral closed restriction theorem gives bijectivity of sections for every Zariski sheaf of sets. Use h=id for X itself, and arbitrary finite h for every finite cover. Apply Gabber's degree-zero criterion to obtain bijective restriction of every etale sheaf of sets. The value universe may be u+1: the proof of spectral restriction uses finite constant sheaves and filtered colimits and does not require the values to have the same universe as the space.

source.place: Lemma 59.82.2; spectral input at Tag 09ZG, Lemma 59.82.4

proof.text: Apply the set-valued conclusion to the underlying sheaf of F. Etale inverse image preserves finite products and acts on algebraic structure maps, compatibly with the inverse-image adjunction unit. The same construction acts on addition and on each scalar operation of a Lambda-module. Equivalently, its presheaf construction uses filtered colimits (the etale neighbourhood index is filtered via finite fibre products and equalizers), for which the underlying-set functor on modules creates colimits; sheafification's matching families carry pointwise module operations. Thus module inverse image and its unit forget to set inverse image and its unit. Evaluation on the terminal object, followed by the terminal-base-change isomorphism and the global-sections identification, identifies the underlying function of globalSectionsUpperStarMap with the bijection in the preceding step. The inverse of a bijective module map preserves addition and scalar multiplication: apply the original injective map to both sides of each proposed identity. This constructs an inverse in ModuleCat and proves IsIso.
